newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati plans commemoration, despite ban.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati plans commemoration, despite ban.

text.p: Supporters of ousted Indonesian minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri said on Saturday they still planned to commemorate the first anniversary of a raid on party offices, despite the event being banned.

Party rivals backed by police and troops raided the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) headquarters in Jakarta on July 27 last year to evict Megawati supporters who had occupied the building after her government-backed ouster a month earlier.

The raid sparked rioting in which the official National Commission of Human Rights reported at least five people died, 23 went missing and 149 were injured. It criticised the interference of security forces in political matters.
Megawati plans to hold a prayer gathering at her house in south Jakarta on Saturday night and lay wreaths at the party offices, still boarded up and under repair, on Sunday morning.
"Up to now we are still planning to go ahead with our plans," Megawati loyalist Haryanto Taslam told Reuters on Saturday morning.
Megawati issued a message, received by Reuters on Saturday, calling on PDI members and supporters to remember "Gray Saturday July 27, 1996" peacefully.
"Avoid and don't be provoked by certain parties who intentionally want to cause chaos and trigger disturbances," Megawati wrote.

Witnesses said on Saturday there did not appear to be any build-up of police or troops near the headquarters, although some Jakarta newspapers had reported armoured cars and riot police on duty at the site in recent days.

Police have refused to give permission for any commemoration ceremony at the site, saying they have banned such a gathering, but organisers have said they only needed to give police notice of their plans and did not need to ask permission.
"Those who violate the law must be subject to order and firm action," Jakarta police chief Major-General Hamami Nata was quoted by Saturday's Kompas daily as telling reporters on Friday.
The newspaper also quoted Jakarta military commander Major-General Sutiyoso as saying on Friday that those who planned to lay wreaths would be dispersed because it was illegal.
Army chief-of-staff General Wiranto was quoted as saying there was no need for any commemoration.
"The July 27 event does not need to be commemorated but instead needs to be regretted because already it has caused much loss to the community," he said.
Hundreds of vehicles were burned by rioters and a number of government buildings, banks and car showrooms were set ablaze in the worst rioting in Jakarta in more than 20 years.
Despite her ousting, Megawati still has considerable influence over PDI supporters as demonstrated during the May general elections, in which she was barred from participating.
Analysts say her public pronouncement that she would not vote led to a collapse of the PDI vote from about 15 percent to around three percent nationally.

The ruling Golkar party won the poll with a record majority in excess of 74 percent, while the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) picked up the balance. Only the three parties were permitted to contest the poll.
